Subject: Dedicated pool — help sizing & GPU options

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We're progressing our internal evaluation for dedicated inference capacity and need some concrete guidance for the next procurement meeting. High level:
- Production workload: multimodal assistant + code generation for internal tools; 800–1,200 concurrent sessions, average 800 tokens/session per minute peak.
- Prefer 99th percentile latency targets < 200ms for text gen and < 400ms for multimodal requests.
- Data residency in us-west region.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) Perf/$ tradeoffs for A100 vs H100 vs L40S for mixed workloads (inference throughput per GPU, typical token/sec for gen workloads, memory headroom).
2) Recommended pool sizing for 12-month reserved commit to hit SLA with 20% headroom.
3) What discounts or pricing tiers exist for 12 vs 24 month commits and for committing at scale (>= 32 GPUs)?
4) Any constraints on model families (quantized vs fp16) that affect throughput guarantees?

Appreciate anything concise we can present to leadership this Thursday.

Thanks,
Donna

Donna — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a concise pricing sheet and our pool-sizing workbook. I pulled initial numbers below that reflect typical production mixes; I'll loop in Karthik for perf-level detail.

Quick summary (high level):
- A100 (40GB): best for fp16/amp workloads; strong perf/$ for medium batch sizes; lower upfront cost than H100 but lower peak throughput on huge attention-heavy models.
- H100 (80GB): higher throughput for large context lengths and high parallelism — better perf/$ if you need fewer GPUs and want to push the latency envelope.
- L40S (48GB): Nvidia L40S gives excellent inference latency for certain vision-heavy models and has good perf/$ for multimodal pipelines when models fit.

Initial recommended commit sizing for your 800–1,200 concurrent sessions (ballpark):
- Conservative (A100): 32 x A10040GB (12-month) with autoscale burst to 40 for peaks; expected to meet 99p latency with 20% headroom.
- Balanced (L40S mix): 24 x L40S + 8 x A100 for vision-heavy peaks.
- Aggressive (H100): 16 x H10080GB with model quantization — fewer GPUs but higher base commit.

Discounts: 12-month commits start at 15% off list for >=16 GPUs, step to 22% for >=32, and 28%+ for bespoke enterprise contract (incl SLA + 24/7 support). 24-months typically get 3–5% additional. Exact numbers in sheet.

Attaching: redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf; acme_pool_commit_calc.xlsx

I'll let Karthik and Monica provide perf numbers and any limits on model variants.

Best,

Rishi / Monica — quick internal note before I send back numbers to Donna. Below are measured ballpark metrics from our perf lab across the models you described (mixed text+vision). These assume our optimized runtime, continuous batching, and KV-cache enabled.

- Small-to-medium LLMs (7B–13B) fp16 quantized:
  * A10040GB: ~280–400 tokens/sec per GPU (single-session-optimized, low-latency batch sizes)
  * H10080GB: ~420–600 tokens/sec per GPU
  * L40S48GB: ~260–380 tokens/sec per GPU (vision calls slightly higher if batch batching applied)

- Large LLMs (70B+):
  * A10040GB: memory constrained; needs model sharding or q4_0 flows — effective tokens/sec ~120–180
  * H10080GB: can run larger variants without sharding; ~240–350 tokens/sec

Notes on perf/$ and memory:
- H100's larger HBM and new attention kernels give near 1.4–1.6x raw throughput vs A100 on large-context workloads. That compresses perf/$ if you can consolidate models onto fewer H100s.
- A100 continues to win on unit price (capex amortized into our pricing) — for workloads dominated by 7B–13B models it's often more economical to scale horizontally.
- L40S shines for multimodal vision encoders: video/imagenet-style encoders have better mem footprint and lower latency; for text-only heavy workloads it's not as cost-efficient as H100.

Operational constraints:
- Quantized variants (q4_0, q5_k) provide ~1.5–2x throughput gains but we only provide throughput guarantees for supported quantization paths listed in the SLA attachment (attached in Rishi's email).
- Autoscale burst policies: we can guarantee baseline throughput at commit level; bursts are best-effort unless included in higher-tier SLA.

I'll draft a short table for Rishi to forward.

—Karthik
Senior Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Donna — following up with a concise recommendation and an initial commercial offer so you have something to present. See key points below and attached pricing sheet.

Proposed configuration (for 12-month reserved commit):
Option A (cost-conscious): 32 x A10040GB
  - Expected baseline throughput: ~9–12k tokens/sec aggregate
  - Estimated 99p latency: <200ms for text workloads with caching
  - List price: $X/GPU-hour; committed price (12mo, >=32): -22%
  - Autoscale burst to 40 GPUs for 2 hours/day

Option B (balanced multimodal): 24 x L40S48GB + 8 x A100
  - Better perf for vision-heavy pipelines; similar agg throughput to A but better latency for multimodal ops
  - Committed discount: -22% with 12mo

Option C (performance-dense): 16 x H10080GB
  - Higher single-GPU throughput; lower total GPUs — good if you want operational simplicity and fewer nodes to manage
  - Committed discount: -18% (H100 premium hardware), 24mo term can push to -23%

Commercial notes:
- Standard 12-month commit pricing bands in sheet; higher discounts available for enterprise contract including penalty-backed SLOs.
- Throughput guarantees: baseline covered by the commit band; burst behavior and additional headroom require the enterprise SLA add-on.
- Model variants: we support specified quantization paths; throughput guarantees only apply to supported variants.

Next steps: if you can confirm target option (A/B/C) and a ballpark GPU count, I can issue a formal quote (including draft MSA and SLA) by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
